body.statement:
Let \(H\in\mathbb S_+^K\) and \(\Omega\in\mathfrak K^{\mathrm{bal}}_{N,K}\).  Put \(J=\mathcal A\times\{1,\ldots,N-1\}\).  For \(\pi\in\mathfrak S_N\) and \(\sigma\in\mathfrak S_N^K\), define the symmetric \(|J|\times|J|\) matrix \(B^{\pi,\sigma}\) by
\[
 B^{\pi,\sigma}_{(a,r),(b,s)}
 =\frac{H_{ab}}{N^2}\sum_{i,j=1}^N\Omega_{ab,\pi(i),\pi(j)}
 \left[(d_r)_i(d_s)_j-(d_r)_{\sigma_a(i)}(d_s)_{\sigma_b(j)}\right].
\]
Then \(\Omega^\pi\in\mathcal C_{N,K}(H)\) if and only if \(B^{\pi,\sigma}\) is copositive for every \(\sigma\), meaning \(u^{\mathsf T}B^{\pi,\sigma}u\geq0\) for every \(u\in\mathbb R_+^J\).  Consequently,
\[
 [\Omega]_{\cong}\in\mathfrak C^{\mathrm{bal}}_{N,K}(H)
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \text{there exists }\pi\in\mathfrak S_N\text{ such that every }B^{\pi,\sigma}\text{ is copositive}.
\]
For any real symmetric matrix \(B\) indexed by \(J\), copositivity has the finite support characterization
\[
 B\text{ is copositive}
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \ker\{B[I]-\lambda I_I\}\cap\mathbb R_{++}^{I}=\varnothing
\]
for every nonempty \(I\subseteq J\) and every negative real eigenvalue \(\lambda<0\) of the principal matrix \(B[I]\).

If, in addition, the entries of \(H\) and \(\Omega\) are supplied as exact real-algebraic numbers, in particular as rational numbers, these equivalences give a finite exact recognition algorithm.  It enumerates \(\pi\), \(\sigma\), and nonempty \(I\), isolates every negative algebraic eigenvalue of \(B^{\pi,\sigma}[I]\), and decides by exact ordered-field linear feasibility whether its eigenspace meets \(\mathbb R_{++}^{I}\).  A noncopositivity certificate consists of \((I,\lambda,v)\) with \(v\in\ker\{B^{\pi,\sigma}[I]-\lambda I_I\}\cap\mathbb R_{++}^{I}\); it yields explicit ordered columns with at most \(N\) levels and a strict loss improvement.  A certificate that a fixed \(\pi\) works consists of the finite collection of infeasibility certificates for all these negative-eigenspace tests.  Thus a yes instance returns such a \(\pi\), while a no instance returns, for every \(\pi\), a corresponding strict cut witness.  No algebraic enumeration claim is made for unrestricted real inputs, and the exhaustive algorithm is not asserted to run in polynomial time.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(\pi\) and \(\sigma\).  Every \(x^a\in\mathcal M_N\) has the unique adjacent-increment representation
\[
 x^a=x_1^a\mathbf 1_N+\sum_{r=1}^{N-1}\alpha_{ar}d_r,
 \qquad \alpha_{ar}=x^a_{r+1}-x^a_r\geq0.
\]
By Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}admissible\text{-}balanced\text{-}kernel}\), \(\sum_i\Omega_{abij}=\sum_j\Omega_{abij}=0\).  These identities are preserved by the common relabelling \(\pi\), so every term containing a constant vector vanishes from both \(\mathscr L_{H,\Omega^\pi}(x,\mathrm{id})\) and \(\mathscr L_{H,\Omega^\pi}(x,\sigma)\).  Substitution of the increment representations into Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}balanced\text{-}kernel\text{-}loss}\) gives, exactly,
\[
 \mathscr L_{H,\Omega^\pi}(x,\mathrm{id})
 -\mathscr L_{H,\Omega^\pi}(x,\sigma)
 =\sum_{(a,r),(b,s)\in J}\alpha_{ar}
 B^{\pi,\sigma}_{(a,r),(b,s)}\alpha_{bs}
 =\alpha^{\mathsf T}B^{\pi,\sigma}\alpha. \tag{4}
\]
The covariance symmetry \(\Omega_{abij}=\Omega_{baji}\), symmetry of \(H\), and interchange of \((a,r,i)\) with \((b,s,j)\) show that \(B^{\pi,\sigma}\) is symmetric.  Conversely, every \(\alpha\in\mathbb R_+^J\) defines ordered columns by taking \(x_1^a=0\) and the displayed cumulative sums.  Therefore (4) proves
\[
 \mathscr L_{H,\Omega^\pi}(x,\mathrm{id})\geq
 \mathscr L_{H,\Omega^\pi}(x,\sigma)\text{ for every }x
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 B^{\pi,\sigma}\text{ is copositive}.
\]
Taking the conjunction over the finite set \(\mathfrak S_N^K\), then the disjunction over \(\pi\in\mathfrak S_N\), proves the first two assertions from Definitions \(\mathrm{def{:}identity\text{-}optimal\text{-}kernel\text{-}cone}\), \(\mathrm{def{:}unit\text{-}relabeling\text{-}equivalence}\), and \(\mathrm{def{:}admissible\text{-}rank\text{-}kernel\text{-}domain}\).

It remains to prove the support criterion.  If a principal matrix \(B[I]\) has \(B[I]v=\lambda v\) for \(\lambda<0\) and \(v\in\mathbb R_{++}^I\), extending \(v\) by zero outside \(I\) gives a nonnegative vector \(\widetilde v\) with
\[
 \widetilde v^{\mathsf T}B\widetilde v
 =v^{\mathsf T}B[I]v=\lambda\lVert v\rVert_2^2<0,
\]
so \(B\) is not copositive.

Conversely, suppose \(B\) is not copositive.  The compact set
\[
 \mathcal D=\{u\in\mathbb R_+^J:\lVert u\rVert_2=1\}
\]
contains a minimizer \(u^*\) of the continuous function \(u\mapsto u^{\mathsf T}Bu\), and its minimum \(\lambda=(u^*)^{\mathsf T}Bu^*\) is negative.  Let \(I=\{j:u_j^*>0\}\).  The vector \(u_I^*\) lies in the relative interior of the positive orthant on the unit sphere in \(\mathbb R^I\).  For every \(w\in\mathbb R^I\) with \(w^{\mathsf T}u_I^*=0\), both signs of a sufficiently small tangent perturbation remain positive on \(I\); first-order minimality therefore gives
\[
 w^{\mathsf T}B[I]u_I^*=0.
\]
Thus \(B[I]u_I^*\) is parallel to \(u_I^*\).  Taking the inner product with \(u_I^*\) identifies the multiplier as \(\lambda<0\), so
\[
 B[I]u_I^*=\lambda u_I^*,
 \qquad u_I^*\in\mathbb R_{++}^I.
\]
This proves the equivalence using every negative real eigenvalue, not merely the sign of the spectrum of the full matrix.

Under the additional exact real-algebraic input hypothesis, every entry of every \(B^{\pi,\sigma}[I]\), every coefficient of its characteristic polynomial, and every eigenvalue is real algebraic.  Passing the finitely many input numbers to a common primitive-element representation, square-free factorization followed by exact sign-variation bisection produces disjoint rational isolating intervals for every real root; exact sign determination then identifies all negative eigenvalues.  Every operation is an exact field operation or a sign test on an algebraic number, and degrees decrease in the Euclidean remainder sequence, so this root-isolation procedure terminates.  For a fixed negative eigenvalue \(\lambda\), homogeneity gives
\[
 \ker\{B[I]-\lambda I_I\}\cap\mathbb R_{++}^I\ne\varnothing
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \exists v:\ (B[I]-\lambda I_I)v=0,\quad v_j\geq1\ (j\in I). \tag{5}
\]
Indeed, a strictly positive vector can be scaled by the reciprocal of its smallest coordinate, and the reverse implication is immediate.  The right side of (5) is a finite linear-feasibility problem over an ordered field of real algebraic numbers.  Eliminate equalities by exact Gaussian operations, and then eliminate each remaining variable by pairing every lower affine bound with every upper affine bound.  Each elimination produces finitely many inequalities and preserves feasibility in both directions; induction on the number of variables reduces the question to finitely many exact sign tests.  Back-substitution returns a feasible algebraic vector, while the incompatible lower--upper pairings give an exact infeasibility certificate.  Since the sets of \(\pi\), \(\sigma\), \(I\), and eigenvalues are finite, the stated algorithm terminates.

When (5) is feasible, extend \(v\) by zero to \(\alpha\in\mathbb R_+^J\) and set
\[
 x_i^a=\sum_{r<i}\alpha_{ar}.
\]
Each column is ordered and has no more than \(N\) distinct values.  Equations (4) and (5) yield
\[
 \mathscr L_{H,\Omega^\pi}(x,\mathrm{id})
 -\mathscr L_{H,\Omega^\pi}(x,\sigma)
 =\lambda\lVert v\rVert_2^2<0,
\]
which is the promised exact strict witness.  Exhausting all tests gives the stated yes and no certificates.  The enumeration includes \((N!)^{K+1}(2^{K(N-1)}-1)\) permutation-support combinations before eigenvalue multiplicities are counted, so this proof supplies only a finite exact algorithm and makes no polynomial-time claim.
body.justification: The theorem gives the computable side of the nonexchangeable extension: universal monotone-column inequalities reduce exactly to finitely many principal-eigenspace feasibility tests.
body.gap: Its exhaustive algorithm does not establish polynomial complexity, and its multilevel failure witnesses do not settle binary completeness or the least complete alphabet.
body.consumer: Small balanced designs with exact rational kernels can be audited exactly, with a relabelling certificate on success or explicit ordered columns and an improving permutation on failure.
